english: Let $f:[0,3]\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=x^{[x]}$ for $x\neq0$ and $f(0)=1$, where $[t]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$. Then $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{3}f(x)\,dx$ is equal to
hindi: माना कि $f:[0,3]\to\mathbb{R}$, $x\neq0$ के लिए $f(x)=x^{[x]}$ तथा $f(0)=1$ द्वारा परिभाषित है, जहाँ $[t]$, $t$ से कम या उसके बराबर महत्तम पूर्णांक को दर्शाता है। तब $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{3}f(x)\,dx$ बराबर है
solution: $[x]$ is constant on $[0,1)$, $[1,2)$, $[2,3)$, so split the integral there (the jumps at $1,2$ do not affect the integral)
solution_full: The greatest integer $[x]$ takes the values $0,1,2$ on $[0,1)$, $[1,2)$, $[2,3)$ respectively, so $f$ is a power function on each of these subintervals; $f$ jumps at $x=1$ and $x=2$ (from $1$ to $1$ at $x=1$, from $2$ to $4$ at $x=2$), and finitely many jumps do not affect the integral.
By additivity, $\int_0^3 f=\int_0^1 f+\int_1^2 f+\int_2^3 f$.
originality_note: New: the greatest integer function is the exponent of a variable base, so each unit interval carries a different power of x (way 2). Closest known: int {x}^[x] dx (fractional part raised to [x], found on allen.in) and int [x] dx counts. Different because: the base is x itself, so each piece is a power integral with different end values, not a harmonic sum.
blueprint_concepts: Additivity over subintervals for piecewise and discontinuous integrands
Definite integrals of GIF and fractional part functions

concept_use.Additivity over subintervals for piecewi: The integral is split at the integers 1 and 2 where f jumps, and the three pieces are added.
concept_use.Definite integrals of GIF and fractional: The greatest integer function sets the exponent: [x] = 0, 1, 2 on the three unit intervals.

justification: Routine chain: identify the three pieces, integrate three powers, add. Slightly more than 2026-P2-Q4 (L1) because the student must track where the exponent changes and the definition at 0.
